activity.notes: Francesco Foscari was elected Doge of Venice in 1423 and remained in office until the Council of Ten forced him to resign in 1457. His dogeship coincided with Venice's major expansion on the Italian mainland. ATLAS models the elected dogeship as governance of the Republic of Venice, not as hereditary kingship.

sources.title: Francesco Foscari — Treccani, Dizionario di Storia
sources.citation_text: Treccani states that Foscari was elected doge in 1423 and forced to leave office in 1457.
